Select the marks in a rectangle or a lasso, by true geometry

Source: R/pick.R
vl_brush.Rd

vl_brush() returns the keyed elements of a scene that meet an axis-aligned rectangle; vl_lasso() those that meet a free-form polygon. Both test the elements' actual geometry – the same recorded shapes vl_nearest() measures – so a diagonal segment is selected only if the line itself enters the region, not because its bounding box does. They are meant for server-side brushing and lasso selection (a Shiny app receiving a brush or lasso from the client) and share one cached spatial index with vl_nearest().

Usage

vl_brush(
  scene,
  xmin,
  xmax,
  ymin,
  ymax,
  units = c("npc", "px"),
  mode = c("intersect", "contain", "centre")
)

vl_lasso(
  scene,
  x,
  y,
  units = c("npc", "px"),
  mode = c("intersect", "contain", "centre")
)

Arguments

scene

A vl_scene() (or anything with an as_vellum_scene() method).

xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax

The rectangle's edges, in units. Their order does not matter.

units

"npc" (default, y up) or "px" (device pixels, y down) — the same convention as hit_test().

mode

"intersect" (default), "contain" or "centre"; see below.

x, y

For vl_lasso(), the polygon's vertices, in units (at least three; the last joins the first).

Value

A data frame of key and kind, one row per selected element, in paint order. A datum drawn as several elements (an error bar's segments) contributes several rows; use unique(res$key) for the selected keys. Only keyed elements are considered.

Which elements are selected

mode decides how an element must meet the region:

  • "intersect" (default): any part of the element touches the region – a point whose disc overlaps it, a line that passes through it, a polygon that overlaps it (including a region wholly inside the polygon). A polygon with a hole does not meet a region that lies entirely in the hole.

  • "contain": all of the element lies inside the region – the whole disc of a point, every vertex of a line or polygon (and, for a lasso, no edge leaving it).

  • "centre": the centre of the element's bounding box lies inside the region. This is the rule vellumwidget's client-side lasso uses, so a server can reproduce a client selection exactly.

Lines and segments are tested along their centre-line, as in vl_nearest(); the stroke width is not added. Elements with nothing drawn (an NA position) are never selected. The lasso polygon is closed implicitly and filled with the even-odd rule, so a self-crossing lasso selects what a client's ray-casting test would.

Performance

The first query on a scene builds a uniform grid over its keyed elements; every later vl_nearest(), vl_brush() or vl_lasso() on the same scene visits only the cells the query touches. The index lives with the compiled scene, so an edited scene (a new object) gets a fresh one.

See also

vl_nearest() for the nearest marks to a point, element_geometry() for the geometry itself.

Examples

s <- vl_scene(4, 3, dpi = 96, bg = "white") |>
  draw(segments_grob(0.1, 0.1, 0.9, 0.9, key = "diagonal")) |>
  draw(points_grob(c(0.2, 0.8), c(0.8, 0.2), key = c("tl", "br")))

# The diagonal's bounding box covers this corner, but the line does not.
vl_brush(s, 0.7, 0.9, 0.1, 0.3)
#>   key  kind
#> 1  br point
vl_brush(s, 0.4, 0.6, 0.4, 0.6)
#>        key    kind
#> 1 diagonal segment

# A triangle around the top-left point
vl_lasso(s, c(0.05, 0.4, 0.05), c(0.6, 0.95, 0.95))
#>   key  kind
#> 1  tl point
